correctness.rationale: Take a degree-d positive-rank divisor D realizing the divisorial gonality of the metric banana path. Corollary 5.3 of arXiv:2609.38821v2 supplies a smooth proper curve X with the same skeleton and genus, together with a degree-d positive-rank divisor B, so gon(X)<=d. For any positive-rank divisor A on X, the Amini--Baker specialization inequality gives positive rank to its tropicalization on the skeleton, with degree preserved, hence deg(A)>=d. Thus gon(X)>=d and equality follows. Theorem 1.1 of the initiating source identifies d with geometric gonality as well.

originality.rationale: The initiating paper states genus-preserving lifting of individual positive-rank divisors on banana paths, but not the exact gonality of the resulting curve. The older general lifting literature either treats specialization inequalities or permits genus increase in general non-augmented gonality lifting, and also exhibits failures in augmented settings. Targeted exact, alias, source, and broader-coverage searches found no statement that every metric banana path has a same-genus algebraic lift of exactly the same gonality.
residual_risks: The exact-gonality upgrade is a short consequence once genus-preserving divisor lifting and specialization are placed together, so it may be implicit in unindexed discussion.
No claim is made that the same curve simultaneously preserves higher gonality-sequence entries.

value.rationale: The result isolates a natural class in which tropical-to-algebraic lifting preserves two basic invariants simultaneously: genus and gonality. This is stronger than merely lifting a positive-rank divisor, because a chosen lift could a priori acquire a lower-degree pencil. It is also stronger than general non-augmented gonality lifting that permits vertex-genus increase, while general augmented exact-gonality lifting is known to fail. The statement therefore gives a reusable structural consequence for the newly introduced banana-path class and immediately turns the source's prescribed-gonality tropical loci into same-genus algebraic curves of exactly that gonality.
